passages.text: Then Elisha said, “Hear the word of the LORD! This is what the LORD says: ‘About this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of the LORD.
Elisha spoke to the people.
Elisha said, “Hear the word of the LORD.
This is what the LORD says.
About this time tomorrow, something will happen at the gate of Samaria.
A seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel.
Two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֑ה כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כָּעֵ֤ת׀ מָחָר֙ סְאָֽה־ סֹ֣לֶת בְּשֶׁ֗קֶל וְסָאתַ֧יִם שְׂעֹרִ֛ים בְּשֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשַׁ֥עַר שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But the officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, “Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?” “You will see it with your own eyes,” replied Elisha, “but you will not eat any of it.”
passages.sermon:
The king had an officer.
The king leaned on this officer’s arm.
Elisha was a man of God.
The officer answered Elisha.
The officer said, “Look, even if the LORD made windows in heaven, could this really happen?”
Elisha replied to the officer.
Elisha said, “You will see it with your own eyes.
But you will not eat any of it.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַן הַשָּׁלִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ לַמֶּלֶךְ֩ נִשְׁעָ֨ן עַל־ יָד֜וֹ אֶת־ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ הִנֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה עֹשֶׂ֤ה אֲרֻבּוֹת֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם הֲיִהְיֶ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנְּכָ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Now there were four men with leprosy at the entrance of the city gate, and they said to one another, “Why just sit here until we die?
passages.sermon:
There were four men.
These men had leprosy.
They sat at the entrance of the city gate.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “Why are we sitting here until we die?”
passages.original: וְאַרְבָּעָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים הָי֥וּ מְצֹרָעִ֖ים פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֔הוּ מָ֗ה אֲנַ֛חְנוּ יֹשְׁבִ֥ים פֹּ֖ה עַד־ מָֽתְנוּ׃

passages.text: If we say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die. So come now, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live; if they kill us, we will die.”
passages.sermon:
Four men had leprosy.
They sat at the entrance of the city gate.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “If we say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ we will die there.
There is a famine in the city.
If we stay here, we will also die.
Now, let us go to the camp of the Arameans.
If they let us live, we will live.
If they kill us, we will die.”
passages.original: אִם־ אָמַרְנוּ֩ נָב֨וֹא הָעִ֜יר וְהָרָעָ֤ב בָּעִיר֙ וָמַ֣תְנוּ שָׁ֔ם וְאִם־ יָשַׁ֥בְנוּ פֹ֖ה וָמָ֑תְנוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה לְכוּ֙ וְנִפְּלָה֙ אֶל־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם אִם־ יְחַיֻּ֣נוּ נִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְאִם־ יְמִיתֻ֖נוּ וָמָֽתְנוּ׃

passages.text: So they arose at twilight and went to the camp of the Arameans. But when they came to the outskirts of the camp, there was not a man to be found.
passages.sermon:
Four men had leprosy.
They sat at the entrance of the city gate.
They got up at twilight.
They went to the camp of the Arameans.
They reached the edge of the Aramean camp.
They saw that no one was there.
passages.original: וַיָּק֣וּמוּ בַנֶּ֔שֶׁף לָב֖וֹא אֶל־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַד־ קְצֵה֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵֽין־ שָׁ֖ם אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: For the Lord had caused the Arameans to hear the sound of chariots, horses, and a great army, so that they said to one another, “Look, the king of Israel must have hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to attack us.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord acted.
The Lord made the Aramean army hear sounds.
They heard the sound of chariots.
They heard the sound of horses.
They heard the sound of a great army.
The Arameans spoke to each other.
They said, “Look, the king of Israel has hired other kings.
He has hired the kings of the Hittites.
He has hired the kings of Egypt.
They are coming to attack us.”
passages.original: וַאדֹנָ֞י הִשְׁמִ֣יעַ׀ אֶת־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֗ם ק֥וֹל רֶ֙כֶב֙ ק֣וֹל ס֔וּס ק֖וֹל חַ֣יִל גָּד֑וֹל וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִ֗יו הִנֵּ֣ה שָֽׂכַר־ עָלֵינוּ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ מַלְכֵ֧י הַחִתִּ֛ים וְאֶת־ מַלְכֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם לָב֥וֹא עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Thus the Arameans had arisen and fled at twilight, abandoning their tents and horses and donkeys. The camp was intact, and they had run for their lives.
passages.sermon:
The Arameans were a foreign army.
They got up at twilight.
They ran away quickly.
They left their tents behind.
They left their horses behind.
They left their donkeys behind.
They left the camp just as it was.
They ran away to save their lives.
passages.original: וַיָּקוּמוּ֮ וַיָּנ֣וּסוּ בַנֶּשֶׁף֒ וַיַּעַזְב֣וּ אֶת־ אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־ סֽוּסֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת־ חֲמֹ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁר־ הִ֑יא וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ אֶל־ נַפְשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: When the lepers reached the edge of the camp, they went into a tent to eat and drink. Then they carried off the silver, gold, and clothing, and went and hid them. On returning, they entered another tent, carried off some items from there, and hid them.
passages.sermon:
Four men had leprosy.
They came to the edge of the Aramean camp.
They entered one tent.
They ate food there.
They drank there.
They took silver from the tent.
They took gold from the tent.
They took clothing from the tent.
They left the tent.
They hid what they had taken.
They returned to the camp.
They entered another tent.
They took more items from that tent.
They left the tent.
They hid those items also.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ הַֽמְצֹרָעִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה עַד־ קְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־ אֹ֤הֶל אֶחָד֙ וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֗ם כֶּ֤סֶף וְזָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ וַיַּטְמִ֑נוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֗בוּ וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־ אֹ֣הֶל אַחֵ֔ר וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ וַיַּטְמִֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Finally, they said to one another, “We are not doing what is right. Today is a day of good news. If we are silent and wait until morning light, our sin will overtake us. Now, therefore, let us go and tell the king’s household.”
passages.sermon:
Four lepers stood at the edge of the Aramean camp.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “We are not doing what is right.
Today is a day of good news.
We are keeping silent.
If we wait until morning light, we will be guilty.
Now, let us go.
Let us tell the king’s household.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֜הוּ לֹֽא־ כֵ֣ן׀ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ עֹשִׂ֗ים הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ יוֹם־ בְּשֹׂרָ֣ה ה֔וּא וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ מַחְשִׁ֗ים וְחִכִּ֛ינוּ עַד־ א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר וּמְצָאָ֣נוּ עָו֑וֹן וְעַתָּה֙ לְכ֣וּ וְנָבֹ֔אָה וְנַגִּ֖ידָה בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So they went and called out to the gatekeepers of the city, saying, “We went to the Aramean camp and no one was there—not a trace—only tethered horses and donkeys, and the tents were intact.”
passages.sermon:
Four lepers went to the city gate.
They called out to the gatekeepers.
They spoke to the gatekeepers.
They said, “We went to the camp of the Arameans.
No one was there.
We did not hear any human voices.
We saw only horses tied up.
We saw donkeys tied up.
The tents were still standing.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֮ אֶל־ שֹׁעֵ֣ר הָעִיר֒ וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֚אנוּ אֶל־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵֽין־ שָׁ֛ם אִ֖ישׁ וְק֣וֹל אָדָ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם־ הַסּ֤וּס אָסוּר֙ וְהַחֲמ֣וֹר אָס֔וּר וְאֹהָלִ֖ים כַּאֲשֶׁר־ הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported to the king’s household.
passages.sermon:
The gatekeepers heard the news.
The gatekeepers shouted the news.
The gatekeepers told the news to others.
People reported the news inside the king’s house.
The king’s household received the news.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֖א הַשֹּֽׁעֲרִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֕ידוּ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ פְּנִֽימָה׃

passages.text: So the king got up in the night and said to his servants, “Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the field, thinking, ‘When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and enter the city.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel got up at night.
He spoke to his servants.
He said, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us.
The Arameans know we are starving.
They left their camp.
They are hiding in the field.
They think, 'When the people come out of the city, we will capture them alive.
Then we will enter the city.'"
passages.original: וַיָּ֨קָם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לַ֗יְלָה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֔יו אַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֣א לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָ֥שׂוּ לָ֖נוּ אֲרָ֑ם יָדְע֞וּ כִּי־ רְעֵבִ֣ים אֲנַ֗חְנוּ וַיֵּצְא֤וּ מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ לְהֵחָבֵ֤ה בְהַשָּׂדֶה לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־ יֵצְא֤וּ מִן־ הָעִיר֙ וְנִתְפְּשֵׂ֣ם חַיִּ֔ים וְאֶל־ הָעִ֖יר נָבֹֽא׃

passages.text: But one of his servants replied, “Please, have scouts take five of the horses that remain in the city. Their plight will be no worse than all the Israelites who are left here. You can see that all the Israelites here are doomed. So let us send them and find out.”
passages.sermon:
One of the king’s servants spoke.
He answered the king.
He said, “Please let men take five of the horses that remain in the city.
These horses are among the last that are left here.
The horses are in the same condition as all the people of Israel who remain in the city.
All the people of Israel who are left here are in danger of dying.
Let us send the men with the horses.
Let us see what happens.”
passages.original: וַיַּעַן֩ אֶחָ֨ד מֵעֲבָדָ֜יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר וְיִקְחוּ־ נָ֞א חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה מִן־ הַסּוּסִים֮ הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ־ בָהּ֒ הִנָּ֗ם כְּכָל־ הֶהָמוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ־ בָ֔הּ הִנָּ֕ם כְּכָל־ הֲמ֥וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־ תָּ֑מּוּ וְנִשְׁלְחָ֖ה וְנִרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then the scouts took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, “Go and see.”
passages.sermon: The scouts took two chariots with horses.\r\nThe king sent the scouts after the Aramean army.\r\nThe king said, "Go and see."
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֕וּ שְׁנֵ֖י רֶ֣כֶב סוּסִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֧י מַחֲנֵֽה־ אֲרָ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר לְכ֥וּ וּרְאֽוּ׃

passages.text: And they tracked them as far as the Jordan, and indeed, the whole way was littered with the clothing and equipment the Arameans had thrown off in haste. So the scouts returned and told the king.
passages.sermon:
The scouts followed the Arameans.
They went as far as the Jordan River.
They saw the whole road.
The road was full of clothing and equipment.
The Arameans had thrown these things away quickly as they fled.
The scouts returned.
They told the king what they saw.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם֮ עַד־ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה כָל־ הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ מְלֵאָ֤ה בְגָדִים֙ וְכֵלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ הִשְׁלִ֥יכוּ אֲרָ֖ם בְּהֵחָפְזָם וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. It was then that a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley sold for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people of Samaria went out.
They found the camp of the Arameans empty.
The people plundered the camp.
They took what the Arameans left behind.
A seah of fine flour sold for one shekel.
Two seahs of barley sold for one shekel.
This happened just as the LORD had said.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָעָ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֕זּוּ אֵ֖ת מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֑ם וַיְהִ֨י סְאָה־ סֹ֜לֶת בְּשֶׁ֗קֶל וְסָאתַ֧יִם שְׂעֹרִ֛ים בְּשֶׁ֖קֶל כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose arm he leaned to be in charge of the gate, but the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, just as the man of God had foretold when the king had come to him.
passages.sermon:
The king appointed an officer to be in charge of the gate.
This officer was the one on whose arm the king leaned.
The people trampled the officer in the gateway.
The officer died.
This happened just as the man of God had foretold.
The man of God spoke this when the king came to him.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֶת־ הַשָּׁלִ֜ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ נִשְׁעָ֤ן עַל־ יָדוֹ֙ עַל־ הַשַּׁ֔עַר וַיִּרְמְסֻ֧הוּ הָעָ֛ם בַּשַּׁ֖עַר וַיָּמֹ֑ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּרֶ֥דֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: It happened just as the man of God had told the king: “About this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria, two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to the king.
Elisha said, “Tomorrow at this time, at the gate of Samaria, two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel.
A seah of fine flour will also sell for a shekel.”
This happened just as Elisha, the man of God, had said.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּדַבֵּר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר סָאתַ֨יִם שְׂעֹרִ֜ים בְּשֶׁ֗קֶל וּֽסְאָה־ סֹ֙לֶת֙ בְּשֶׁ֔קֶל יִהְיֶה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֔ר בְּשַׁ֖עַר שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: And the officer had answered the man of God, “Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?” So Elisha had replied, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it!”
passages.sermon:
The officer served the king.
The king leaned on this officer’s arm.
The man of God was Elisha.
Elisha spoke God’s word.
The officer answered Elisha.
He said, “Look, even if the LORD made windows in heaven, could this really happen?”
Elisha replied to the officer.
He said, “You will see it with your own eyes.
But you will not eat any of it.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׁלִ֜ישׁ אֶת־ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה עֹשֶׂ֤ה אֲרֻבּוֹת֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם הֲיִהְיֶ֖ה כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנְּךָ֤ רֹאֶה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: And that is just what happened to him. The people trampled him in the gateway, and he died.
passages.sermon:
The officer had doubted the word of Elisha, the man of God.
Elisha had said the officer would see the miracle but not eat from it.
It happened just as Elisha said.
The people trampled the officer at the city gate.
He died.
passages.original: וַיְהִי־ ל֖וֹ כֵּ֑ן וַיִּרְמְס֨וּ אֹת֥וֹ הָעָ֛ם בַּשַּׁ֖עַר וַיָּמֹֽת׃ס
